predictions.explanation:
Key points:

1. **Time window not over yet.** The statement was made in an episode published on 6 February 2021. The five‑year horizon therefore runs until around 6 February 2026. As of today (30 November 2025), that window has not expired, so any verdict is technically premature.

2. **The antecedent hasn’t really happened.** Jason’s prediction was conditional: *if* they created an “All‑In Network” of roughly five subject‑focused podcasts (Friedberg on science, Sacks on SaaS, Chamath on public markets, plus All‑In and This Week in Startups), then that network would be “right up there with CNN and MSNBC” within five years. In practice, they have one flagship All‑In podcast plus summits and branded products (e.g., All‑In Summit, All‑In Tequila), not a suite of 4–5 separate recurring subject‑vertical shows under an “All‑In Network” banner.([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-In_%28podcast%29)) Because the specific multi‑show network he described was never built, the conditional is hard to evaluate directly.

3. **All‑In is influential but far smaller than CNN/MSNBC in total audience.** Reporting and profiles describe All‑In as a powerful, agenda‑setting show in tech and politics; a Wall Street Journal piece pegs it at roughly **750,000 views per episode on average**, which is very large for a podcast.([wsj.com](https://www.wsj.com/business/media/silicon-valley-all-in-podcast-01dfadbb?utm_source=openai)) However, CNN and MSNBC still operate as 24‑hour news channels reaching tens of millions of cable households, with average daily audiences in the hundreds of thousands and key shows in the 1–1.5 million viewer range, plus major political events drawing several million viewers per network.([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN?utm_source=openai)) Digitally, they also generate **hundreds of millions to billions** of online video views annually; for example, MSNBC’s Ari Melber alone amassed about **1.5 billion online views in 2024**, and MSNBC has been described as the most‑watched news network on YouTube.([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ari_Melber?utm_source=openai)) This indicates that even if All‑In is “punching above its weight,” its total audience footprint remains well below the combined linear+digital reach of CNN or MSNBC.

4. **Why the verdict is “inconclusive,” not “wrong.”**
   - The **deadline hasn’t passed**, so by your own framing (“within five years…by early February 2026”) there is still some time left.
   - The prediction is explicitly **counterfactual** (about what *would* happen if a particular network of shows were launched), and that condition has not been met, so we cannot empirically test his exact claim.

On present evidence, the concrete scenario Jason sketched (a five‑show All‑In Network rivaling CNN/MSNBC in raw prominence/audience) has **not** materialized so far, and the scale gap remains very large. But because (a) the five‑year period is not over and (b) the triggering “network of five pods” was never actually built, the fairest scoring under your scheme is **“inconclusive (too early)” rather than definitively right or wrong.

predictions.grok_explanation: The predicted 'All-In Network' of roughly five subject-focused podcasts (e.g., Friedberg on science, Chamath on public markets, Sacks on SaaS, plus All-In and This Week in Startups) was never created. Searches for 'All-In Network podcasts Chamath Jason Sacks Friedberg' and related terms yield no evidence of such a network; only the single weekly *All-In Podcast* exists ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-In_(podcast)), [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/all-in-with-chamath-jason-sacks-friedberg/id1502871393), [Spotify Charts](https://podcastcharts.byspotify.com/)). Jason Calacanis maintains his separate *This Week in Startups*, but no unified network launched. Without the network, it cannot be 'right up there' with CNN/MSNBC. Even the main podcast, while popular (top 50 in some US charts like Edison Q2/Q3 2025, Spotify top 50), has far smaller reach than CNN/MSNBC's average primetime viewership of 500k-1.5M total viewers ([Adweek Oct 2025](https://www.adweek.com/tvnewser/here-are-the-cable-news-ratings-for-october-2025/), [Hollywood Reporter Nov 2025](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/msnbc-ratings-election-night-2025-1236419064/)) or their broader daily TV audience/prominence. Nearly 5 years have passed (Feb 2021 to Dec 2025), with no network materializing.

As of November 30, 2025, Green is an active NBA player for the Golden State Warriors and is publicly described as a professional basketball player, not a politician or officeholder. There is no record of him serving as governor of Michigan or California. 【4search14】

Current governors are Gretchen Whitmer in Michigan (in office since January 1, 2019) 【2search14】 and Gavin Newsom in California (in office since January 7, 2019), 【3search13】 confirmed by both Wikipedia and the official California governor website. 【3search0】 Neither office is held by Draymond Green, and historical lists of governors for both states contain no entry for him. 【2search12】【2search13】

Because Green is under 50 and still has time to meet the condition of becoming governor of either Michigan or California before that birthday, the prediction cannot yet be judged as right or wrong. It remains **too early to tell**, so the outcome is **inconclusive**.

predictions.explanation:
It is **too early** to determine whether this prediction is correct.

- The prediction is effectively *lifelong*: that Draymond Green will have California as his primary home "for the rest of my life."
- As of late 2025, Draymond Green is still alive and actively playing in the NBA for the Golden State Warriors, a California-based team .
- There is no reliable public information establishing where his *permanent* primary residence will be for the remainder of his life; future moves or changes of residency cannot be ruled out.

Because the prediction concerns his entire remaining lifetime and that lifetime is ongoing, it **cannot yet be evaluated**. Therefore the status is **inconclusive (too early)** rather than right or wrong.

Possible Bay Area property, still CA. No evidence of leaving CA or non-CA primary home. However, verifying a *lifetime* commitment is too early, as Green (age 35) could relocate later (e.g., retirement). Thus, inconclusive (too early).
